title: Joe Corra
text:
Quantitative Scientist  ·  Data Infrastructure & Environmental Quantification
    
    
      I build reproducible analytical systems for environmental data problems. My work spans
      the design of data pipelines, open-source tooling, and methodology-driven 
      workflows — applied primarily in the climate and GHG emissions space.
    
    
      Currently a Physical Scientist at the U.S. EPA, where I led 
      modernization of data infrastructure supporting the 
      Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks. I work primarily in 
      R, with an emphasis on reproducible workflows, Shiny applications, 
      and Quarto-based reporting.
    
    
      Before moving into climate science, my research and quantitative and work was in avian ecology —
      a background that still shapes how I think about data quality, uncertainty, 
      and methodology.

title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
⬇ Download PDF 


  Summary
  
    Quantitative scientist specializing in the design and development of reproducible 
    analytical systems for environmental data. Core strengths in data pipeline 
    architecture, open-source tooling, and methodology-driven workflows applied in 
    the GHG emissions and climate domain. Domain experience spans HFC and refrigerant 
    accounting, fossil fuel combustion emissions, and reservoir GHG emissions.
  



  Experience

  
    Physical Scientist / Data Scientist
    US EPA, Office of Air and Radiation  ·  Nov 2023 – Present
    
      Built reproducible data pipelines supporting federal GHG reporting under UNFCCC 
      frameworks. Developed emissions estimation tools and data systems for national 
      climate reporting and corporate emissions inventories. Advised on technical design 
      of public-facing inventory tools. Mentored 13 colleagues in R programming.
    
  

  
    Biological Science Technician
    US EPA, Office of Research and Development  ·  May 2021 – Nov 2023
    
      Developed data management plans, QA/QC protocols, and analytical workflows 
      supporting policy-relevant environmental research. Produced visualizations, 
      reports, and manuscripts for scientific and regulatory audiences.
    
  

  
    Utility Analyst (Environmental)
    New York State Department of Public Service  ·  Oct 2019 – Apr 2021
    
      Analyzed renewable energy generation and transmission projects within New York's 
      utility regulatory framework, supporting state decision-making on energy 
      infrastructure investments.
    
  

  
    Avionics Technician (Active Guard Reserve)
    New York Air National Guard, 109th Airlift Wing  ·  Nov 2006 – Aug 2016
  



  Technical Skills
  
    Programming & Data Infrastructure: R (advanced), R Shiny, Quarto, 
    Git/GitHub, automated data pipelines, API integration, web scraping, data validation 
    frameworks, QA/QC workflows, reproducible reporting, LLM integration in R
  
  
    GHG & Climate: Emissions inventory development, HFC/refrigerant 
    accounting, Kigali Amendment / Montreal Protocol, IPCC methodology (Tier 1–3), 
    GHG Protocol (Scope 1/2/3), UNFCCC reporting frameworks, fossil fuel combustion, 
    reservoir emissions
  
  
    Analysis & Visualization: Statistical analysis, ggplot2, 
    interactive dashboards, technical report writing
  



  Education
  
    MS, Environment and Natural Resources
    The Ohio State University  ·  2019
  
  
    BS, Science, Mathematics, and Technology

    Concentration: Environmental Science
  
  
    AAS, Avionics Systems Technology
    Community College of the Air Force  ·  2011

title: Projects
text:
A collection of open-source tools and analytical infrastructure for environmental data quantification, reproducible workflows, and GHG inventory methods.


  
    R Package
    Syrinx
    
      Data quality control infrastructure for GHG inventory workflows. Uses a 
      data dictionary-driven approach and LLM-assisted harmonization to standardize 
      character data across heterogeneous inventory sources, with utilities supporting 
      reproducible, audit-ready pipelines.
    
    
      GitHub →
      
    
  

  
    R Shiny
    HFC Reporting Tool
    
      Open-source Shiny application enabling developing countries to compile 
      Kigali Amendment HFC consumption data into IPCC-compliant emissions estimates. 
      Produces time-series estimates by gas and application sector across Tier 1–3 
      methodology.
    
    
      GitHub →
      
    
  

  
    Claude Skill
    GHG Methodology Narrator
    
      A Claude skill that translates R scripts implementing GHG inventory 
      methodology into plain-language narratives readable by domain experts 
      who are not R programmers. Designed for peer review and documentation 
      of reproducible inventory workflows.
    
    
      GitHub →
    
  

  
    Claude Skill
    GHG Methodology Parser
    
      Parses narrative methodology descriptions from GHG inventory documents 
      into structured, language-agnostic implementation frameworks — bridging 
      the gap between methodology text and reproducible code.
    
    
      GitHub →
    
  

  
    Claude Skill
    R GHG Coder
    
      Translates structured GHG inventory implementation frameworks into 
      production-ready R code following established conventions for reproducible, 
      audit-ready inventory workflows.
    
    
      GitHub →
